seo.title: Cura — Evidence Automation for Airline Operations

hero.title:
Your OCC stops being
the evidence archive.
hero.sub: Months after a disruption, an authority asks for the NOTAMs, the slot messages, the delay codes and the duty manager's notes — and the request lands on your desk. Cura pulls every one of those sources over an API the moment the request arrives, drafts the response in the authority's own structure and files it. Nobody in operations is asked for anything.

nodes.title: Evidence collected
nodes.body: Weather, NOTAMs, CTOT, delay codes, booking — pulled in parallel

nodes.title: Response drafted
nodes.body: Cause categorised, delay attributed minute by minute

pain.title: Every escalation ends the same way: someone in operations digging through March.
pain.body: A national authority writes to the airline eleven weeks after the flight. Legal cannot answer it without you — so the request becomes a favour, then a chase, then a deadline.

compare.title: The request never reaches your team.
compare.body: Same escalation, same authority, same deadline — a completely different week for the people running the operation.

now.title: Evidence is assembled by memory, months late.

items.text: Legal emails OCC asking what happened on a flight from three months ago.
NOTAMs, CTOTs and weather have to be reconstructed from whatever was saved on the day.
The duty manager who worked that shift may not be the one answering.
Thin evidence means paying claims the airline should have defended.

cura.title: Evidence is sealed at the moment of the disruption.

items.text: Every source is fetched over an API the moment the request lands — in parallel, in minutes.
Weather, minima and NOTAMs are stamped at the time of the disruption, not recalled later.
No one in OCC is interrupted. The read-only API is wired up once, at onboarding.
The airline defends what it can defend, on the record, with a checksum per document.

nodes.title: Read and matched
list: Claim found — matched to the case on file
No claim — new case is opened

learning.title: It gets better with every case.
learning.body: Three signals feed back into the drafting agent — two from day one, one when the rulings land.

cards.title: Edit diffs
cards.body: Every paragraph an agent rewrites. Eight rewrites in ten is a template problem — fixed the same day.

cards.title: Overrides
cards.body: Every time an agent pays against a defend call, with the reason. Expert judgement, months before the verdicts.

cards.title: Rulings
cards.body: Parsed argument by argument: dismissed in 11 of 14 cases resting on an operations log alone.

note.text: Counting, not training. Rates you can inspect, trace to real cases and defend in a dispute — not a model nobody can explain to a regulator.

cta.title: See it run on one of your own flights.
